name: Arizona State University
description: In the heart of Tempe, ASU is a key factor in its vibrant, diverse and progressive lifestyle. It was founded as a Normal (Teaching) school in 1885. Arizona State is now one of the largest universities in the nation, with several campuses spread throughout the metropolitan area. The largest of these…

name: Old Main
description: The original school's building, dating back to its founding.

name: Gammage Memorial Auditorium
description: A theater designed by Frank Lloyd Wright that hosts international talent, Broadway shows, and local entertainment. One of his last architectural pieces, it was designed for Baghdad before being built in the equally arid Valley of the Sun.

name: ASU Mars Space Flight Facility
description: Supports the Thermal Emission Spectrometer experiment that was sent aboard the Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft when it launched in November 1996. The Mars facility has a visitor area with displays about Mars and a television tuned to NASA TV.

name: ASU Robert S. Dietz Museum of Geology
description: Houses minerals, gems, fossils from Arizona and around the world. It also has a six-story Foucault pendulum; local fossils including Colombian mammoth remains excavated in 1985, 1997 and 1999; real dinosaurs, a giant-extinct fossil shark over 7 ft (2.1 m) tall (featured on the National Geographic…

name: ASU Center for Meteorite Studies
description: Houses the world's largest university-based meteorite collection, with specimens from more than 1700 separate meteorite falls. Portions of this collection are on display to the public.

name: ASU Art Museum
description: Has a fine permanent collection and an active guest artist program. The attached gift shop is, surprisingly, a great place to get beautiful and unusual gifts.

name: Hayden Library
description: A vast collection housed mostly underground in the center of campus. It has many unique features, including the only Child Drama collection, various exhibits, and rare and valuable works available to the public through the Luhrs reading room. Where else can one walk in and request to see a page…

name: Life Sciences Tower
description: Has glass cases set into the hallways that house dozens of reptiles, including a comprehensive sampling of the poisonous snakes of Arizona.

name: ASU Museum of Anthropology
description: Run by the internationally acclaimed School of Human Evolution and Social Change, has many interesting permanent and visiting exhibits throughout the year.

name: Northlight Gallery
description: Exhibits a broad range of photographic work by emerging and international recognized artists.
hours: Tue 12:30-8:30PM, Wed-Sat 12:30-4:30PM; closed on major holidays and in summer

name: AZ Heritage Center at Papago Park
description: A museum that concentrates on Arizona's history in the 20th and 21st centuries.

name: Tempe History Museum
description: Features the history of Tempe from the time of prehistoric Hohokam to today. Video, hands-on exhibits and gift shop.

name: City of Tempe Cultural Services Public Art
description: Numerous examples of public art dot Tempe's landscape. Additionally, Tempe presents exhibits featuring professional and student artists. Works may be viewed in public places, which serve as alternate spaces for regularly changing exhibits.

name: Petersen House Museum
description: Restored Queen Anne Victorian home built in 1892 by one of Tempe's earliest settlers.

name: Tempe Center for the Arts
description: For events see the event calendar .

name: Salt River Project History Center
description: Has exhibits illustrating the construction of the Theodore Roosevelt Dam, as well as other exhibits relating to the history of water usage in Arizona.

name: Sea Life Arizona
description: Has a walk-through aquarium, and 30 displays.
price: $12 online/$18 at gate (adults 13+), $12 online/$13 at gate (children 3-12)

name: Tempe Town Lake
description: Set adjacent to Tempe's Mill Avenue District, Arizona State University and the 2,000 acres (810 hectares) Papago Park, Tempe Town Lake embodies a unique vision for the future of the Valley. It is the center for many activities like boating, biking etc and has a jogger's track as well. The sight of…

name: Ironman Arizona
description: Held annually in November.

name: P.F. Chang's Rock'n'Roll Arizona Marathon and Half Marathon
description: Held annually in January.

name: Buffalo Wild Wings Bowl
description: Annually in December.

name: Angels Major League Baseball Spring Training
description: Hosted every March.

name: Tempe Festival of the Arts
description: Massive twice yearly street fair featuring arts and crafts from all over the country, as well as a wide selection of carnival/street fair style foods, beverages and live entertainment. Held at the end of March and beginning of December.

name: Cafe Lalibela
description: Cafe Lalibela is a family restaurant bringing Ethiopian cuisine to the heart of Tempe. Takeout available.
hours: Mon-Thu 11AM-9PM, Fri 11AM-10PM, Sat noon-10PM, Sun noon-9PM

name: Cornish Pasty Co
description: A British and Irish themed restaurant and bar offers a wide range of classic, modern, and experimental pasties with a number of European beers available on tap. It is popular with Tempe's younger and bohemian crowd.

name: Green New American Vegetarian
description: Vegan restaurant that was named the best vegan restaurant in Phoenix by the Phoenix New Times. PETA named the secret BBQ Chicken sandwich as the best faux chicken sandwich in the USA. Another location in Central Phoenix.

name: La Fonda Mexican Food
description: La Fonda is a great restaurant if you're looking for Mexican food. The food is excellent, and the atmosphere is friendly; good pricing is an added benefit, not a factor.

name: Little Szechwan
description: Family-run Chinese restaurant. Mouth-watering food and very friendly service.

name: Munch a Mania
description: The food is wonderful, portion sizes are great, and the service is the most personal you will get in town. Free delivery ($10 minimum order).

name: My Big Fat Greek Restaurant
description: Delivers large portions of Greek food and is a favorite of many ASU college students.

name: Phoenicia Cafe
description: Delicious Mediterranean and Middle Eastern food. Relatively small and often packed, esp. while the university nearby is in session. Try the babaganouj (eggplant dip) and the baklava, made from scratch. There is also an attached small Middle Eastern grocery that has great prices, especially on…

name: Rosita's Fine Mexican Food
description: This popular, long-established family restaurant serves up Mexican classic dishes with a focus on Sonoran cooking.

name: Courtyard Tempe Downtown
description: 10 minute free shuttle ride from your flight into Sky Harbor Airport. From there you are just blocks from downtown Tempe and Arizona State University.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Tempe
description: Rates include free wi-fi and breakfast. 12 mi (19 km) from downtown Phoenix.

name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Phoenix Tempe - University
description: Located within walking distance of ASU, this hotel offers proximity to local area attractions in a room with various full-service accommodations. Includes breakfast and wi-fi.

name: Quality Inn Airport Tempe
description: Centrally located near the airport, ASU, the Mill Avenue District, and Tempe Town Lake. Pets accepted.

name: Quality Inn at ASU
description: This hotel is 5 mi (8.0 km) from the airport and very close to ASU. Easy access to freeways for travel in Tempe. Breakfast and wi-fi included.

name: Tempe Mission Palms Hotel
description: Upscale 303-room hotel with courtyard and roof top pool, 30,000 ft² (2,800 m 2 ) of conference space, 10 ADA rooms, restaurant. AAA/CAA & TAG approved.

name: Chapel of the Holy Cross
description: This unique chapel built into the rock offers great views.

name: Palatki Heritage Site
description: A Sinagua archeological site with cliff dwellings and pictographs and petroglyphs, dated to 1100-1400 CE. The site is located in the Coconino National Forest, and has three interpretive trails. Reservations are recommended, as visitor numbers are managed by the rangers to limit damage to the site.…

name: Honanki Heritage Site
description: A Sinagua cliff dwelling site with numerous pictographs, inhabited from 1100-1300 CE. The site is managed by the Coconino National Forest Service. A Red Rock Pass is required on all vehicles; the passes are not sold here and must be purchased beforehand.

name: Sedona Heritage Museum
description: A small museum dedicated to the history of early white settlement in Sedona.

name: Snoopy rock
description: A rock formation that from the "right side" looks like the Snoopy dog character lying on his back.

name: Boynton Canyon
description: One of the most scenic of the box canyons in the area, and correspondingly popular. The parking lot is a short distance from the trail head; no parking at the luxury resort.

name: Broken Arrow Trail
description: Follow an easy 2-mile hike to Chicken Point. Well-marked trail (follow the cairns). Beautiful views. Do early in the morning before Pink Jeeps - which start around 8AM. Can also see Submarine Rock from trail. This route is popular for mountain biking.

name: Cathedral Rock Trail
description: For a challenge, this 0.8-mile trail is steep, but the view is unparalleled. Great at sunset. Beats Airport Mesa. Can walk around the base of the rock for a less strenuous hike.

name: Bell Rock Pathway / Vista
description: A 3.7-mile trail with fantastic views of Bell Rock, Courthouse Butte, and the surrounding area. Suitable for hiking and mountain biking.

name: Devil's Bridge Trail
description: The largest natural sandstone arch in the area. The trail is short and moderately difficult, with outstanding views at the top. A high-clearance vehicle is recommended.

name: Red Rock State Park
description: This 286-acre preserve was once part of the Smoke Trail Ranch, and has ten well-maintained hiking trails as well as a visitor center. A number of guided hikes, birdwatching walks, and astronomy events are offered.

name: Slide Rock State Park
description: Formerly known as the Pendley Homestead, this historic apple farm is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. It is named for a slippery rock slide into a creek. Swimming encouraged.

name: Oakcreek Country Club
description: An 18-hole golf course.

name: Desert Canyon Loop Scenic Drive
description: This scenic loop begins east of Interstate 17 where State Route 179 from Sedona crosses I17 to become FR618 just north of Camp Verde, Arizona. This scenic drive is a high desert landscape in the vicinity of Montezuma's Well National Monument and Montezuma's Castle National Park.

name: Oak Creek Canyon Scenic Drive
description: Follow 89A through Sedona and Oak Creek Canyon. Beautiful views of dramatic canyon walls through the pine Forest. Oak Creek runs year-round and can be viewed from many points along the route. Hike West Fork of Oak Creek, for a moderate, well-marked 2.5-mi hike, with 6 Creek crossings. Pay to park.

name: Red Rocks and Sycamore Canyon Loop Scenic Drive
description: This drive takes you into the heart of the magnificent Sedona Red Rocks Country. The route traces the base of dramatic cliffs and offers the option of four scenic side trips that lead to some of the most exciting features in Red Rock Country.

name: Red Rock Scenic Byway
description: Beautiful views start on Arizona's First All-American Road, also known as the gateway to Red Rock Country. Exit I-17 and head north. The road ends in Sedona at a traffic circle. On this National Scenic Byway (south of the Village of Oak Creek on SR 179), you'll find the Coconino National Forest…

name: Boynton Canyon
description: A pretty drive up Half-High Rd and left at Enchantment Resort. Nice hike up Boynton Canyon, or 1 mile past resort, at Doe Mountain.

name: A Spa for You Sedona Day Spa & Massage
description: Offers individually created signature massage, body treatments and Japanese facial massage. All sessions include a 15-minute consultation with a massage therapist. By reservation only.

name: Unity of Sedona
description: A New Age spiritual center, new thought church, and energy vortex featuring sacred services, workshops, a labyrinth, psychics, concerts, spiritual gatherings, and a metaphysical bookstore and gift shop. Inspiring and unique Sunday Services at 9:30am and 12:00 noon welcoming all who find their way…

name: Picazzo Pizza
description: Very good food, pizza choices are too numerous to mention. Take out available.

name: Wildflower Bread Company
description: Wildflower raised the bar for affordable dining in Sedona. Good food at affordable prices. Great views of the red rocks. Nice comfortable fireplace on a winters' day, with daily newspapers and free wi-fi. Very central location.

name: Creekside Coffee
description: A cozy coffee shop with an unobstructed view of the surrounding red rocks with a good amount of seating, indoors and out.

name: Casa Bonita
description: They offer a 10% discount if you are staying at a few selected hotels in the area. Just show your room key.
hours: Sun-Thu 11AM-10PM, Fri Sat 11AM-11PM; daily Happy Hour 3-6PM

name: Coffee Pot Restaurant
description: A local institution that has been featured on the Travel Channel, Food Network, etc. With a view of Coffee Pot Rock, this historic family-friendly place offers 101 omelets and southwestern favorites. Open for breakfast and lunch only. Includes a small curio shop.

name: Cowboy Club
description: Very central and very popular steak house. Good atmosphere, food is pretty good. Really don't understand why so popular, but on a weekend plan on a 45 minute wait during evening hours for a table (reservations accepted).

name: Javelina Cantina
description: Large portions of average American-Mexican food with an excellent view from the balcony. Food is good, not great.

name: Ken’s Creekside Restaurant
description: Amazing food and friendly service. The peach cobbler is heavenly!

name: Szechuan Chinese Restaurant & Martini Bar
description: Delivery available.

name: Safeway
description: Has a full-service hot and cold deli, as well as an onsite pharmacy.

name: Sedona.org Vacation Rentals
description: Sedona.org Vacation Rentals offers vacation homes in Sedona with luxury furnishings, high end amenities, and easy access to Sedona's attractions. Book today

name: Porter Vacation Rentals
description: Offering vacation rentals in Sedona.

name: Sky Ranch Lodge
description: Scenic views from Airport Mesa, pet friendly. Nice grounds. Quiet. Older property but well maintained. Reasonable prices.

name: Aiden by Best Western Sedona
description: Basic motel, good location, set back from road. Free wi-fi and breakfast, pool, pet-friendly. Clean.

name: GreenTree Inn Sedona
description: Swimming pool and jacuzzi. Free continental breakfast and wi-fi.

name: Mountain Modern Sedona
description: A pleasant hotel on the outskirts of town, just off 89A. Rooms have exterior entrances; they're a bit on the small side but they're clean and well-decorated. Free hot breakfast with some very good options, and free wi-fi. Concierge and pool; pet-friendly.

name: El Portal Sedona Luxury Hacienda and Restaurant
description: The architecture and adobe construction of El Portal is completely authentic. Nowhere else in Sedona will you find a luxury inn or hotel with 18-inch thick adobe walls— walls that provide both quiet and history. Twelve spacious rooms have been created in accordance with the simplicity and function…

name: Enchantment Resort
description: Pricey, but very nice.

name: The Penrose Inn Bed and Breakfast
description: One of the best. The service, amenities, and delicious, hot breakfasts are miles above average. Their view of Bell Rock and Courthouse Butte is unmatched.

name: The Sedona Dream Maker Bed and Breakfast
description: An extraordinary B&B made of logs and love in a luxury log home.

name: The Wilde Resort and Spa
description: 77-room boutique hotel and spa in West Sedona.

name: Cave Springs Campground
description: Open April - October, this is one of the most popular campgrounds in the area. 82 sites with picnic tables and fire pits, drinking water and toilets, coin-operated showers available. No hookups, trailers under 36'. Reservations can be made online .

name: Manzanita Campground
description: Open year round, with 18 single-unit sites with tables, fire pits, vault toilets, and drinking water. No hookups, 7-day limit. Reservations can be made online . Campers may use the coin-operated showers in Cave Springs Campground (listed above).

name: Pine Flat Campground
description: Open April - October, this is another very popular campground. 56 units are available, 18 of which can be reserved online . Vault toilets, drinking water (no showers), no hookups, trailers under 30'. Campers may use the coin-operated showers at nearby Cave Springs Campground (listed above).

name: Rancho Sedona RV Park
description: Full and partial hookups with 50-amp service.

name: Lowell Observatory
description: An astronomical research center from which the dwarf planet Pluto was discovered, this historic institution is on a mesa overlooking the west side of town. The staff leads guided daytime tours, and visitors use the Observatory's 24" Clark telescope and smaller portable telescopes during regular…

name: Museum of Northern Arizona
description: On the north side of town, it has displays on Native American life and the natural history of the region. A good selection of Native American folk art, particularly Navajo rugs, is available at the gift shop.

name: Arboretum at Flagstaff
description: This 200-acre botanical garden, environmental research station, and nature center displays one of America's largest collections of high country wildflowers. Daily guided tours at 11AM and 1PM. Wild Birds of Prey programs at F-M noon and 2PM.

name: Riordan Mansion State Historic Park
description: This fine example of an Arts and Crafts style house was built in 1904 for a prominent local family. Guided tours are conducted at the top of the hour, reservations recommended.

name: Pioneer Museum
description: This small state museum collects, preserves and exhibits artifacts, documents and photographs of the history of Flagstaff and northern Arizona. It also hosts a number of events throughout the year.

name: Fort Tuthill Military Museum
description: A former National Guard training facility built in 1929, this small museum now has displays devoted to regional military history.
price: $3 (adults 13+), Free (seniors, children, active military, National Guard members)
hours: May-Sep: Thu Fri noon-4PM (based on staff availability), Sat Sun 10AM-4PM

name: Northern Arizona University Art Museum
description: Has rotating exhibits featuring local and international artists.
hours: Tue-Sat noon-5PM during the school year

name: Coconino Center for the Arts
description: The largest gallery in northern Arizona, showcases local and regional art.

name: Elden Pueblo Historic Site
description: A Sinagua archeological site which was inhabited from 1050-1275 CE. An easy interpretive trail circles the ruins. It is managed by the Coconino National Forest Service, which hosts a number of educational programs and workshops at the site.

name: Picture Canyon Natural and Cultural Preserve
Absolute Bikes
description: Mountain bikes can be rented

name: Mount Elden
description: This area is managed by the Coconino National Forest, and is an excellent starting point for exploring the area with numerous trails running up and alongside most faces of the mountain. One of the most popular trails is Elden Lookout Trail , which scales all 2800 ft (855m) from base to summit, and…

name: San Francisco Peaks
description: Managed by the Coconino National Forest, the San Francisco Peaks northwest of Flagstaff offer a number of hiking trails for all skill levels, as well as opportunities for mountain biking, rock climbing, camping, and skiing. The range is crowned by the 12,637-ft Humphreys Peak, and is held sacred by…

name: Arizona Snowbowl
description: Alpine skiing. One of only three ski resorts in the state of Arizona. Despite the surrounding desert, Flagstaff is a popular skiing destination for the Southwest due to the high elevation. Interestingly, the Snowbowl is one of the first ten ski resorts established in the United States. Snowbowl is…

name: Flagstaff Nordic Center
description: One of the southwest's best cross-country skiing areas with over 50 km of well-groom ski trails and 25 km of snowshoe trails. In the summer the trails are open for hiking and mountain biking. Trail passes and equipment rental prices are listed here ; overnight cabin rental is also available.

name: Jay Lively Activity Center
description: City-owned permanent indoor ice skating rink. Offers ice skating lessons, public skating sessions, and also hosts ice hockey games.

name: Northern Arizona Yoga Center
description: Northern Arizona Yoga Center is the largest yoga studio in town. This studio offers more than just yoga: they also host Salsa parties, Tango classes, Capoiera, Pilates, and Tai Chi. They are also a great supplier of yoga clothing and accessories. They are partners with the Vertical Relief Climbing…

name: Flagstaff Extreme Adventure Course
description: A suspended obstacle course with more than 70 aerial challenges for children and adults.

name: Hitchin’ Post Stables
description: Offers guided horseback riding excursions forest land southeast of Flagstaff, ranging from 1 to 8 hours in length.

name: First Friday ArtWalk
description: Every first Friday of the month art galleries and restaurants stay open until late in the evening, with live street entertainment and music centered around Heritage Square.

name: Zuni Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually in late May, this two-day festival sponsored by NAU celebrates Zuni culture with dance and music, and arts and crafts demonstrations and exhibits.

name: Hopi Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually around the third week of August, this festival celebrates Hopi traditions and culture with music, dance, food, and arts and crafts exhibits.

name: Navajo Festival of Arts and Culture
description: Held annually in early August, celebrates Diné (Navajo) culture with music, dance, lectures, food, art, and weaving demonstrations.

name: Celebraciones de la Gente
description: Held in late October, this festival celebrates the Mexican holiday Dia de los Muertos, or Day of the Dead . Activities include mariachi music, storytelling, and arts demonstrations. Ofrendas (private altars) are exhibited in the courtyard.

name: Arizona Highland Celtic Festival
description: Held every July, with music, dance, and food and drink.

name: Pickin' in the Pines Bluegrass & Acoustic Music Festival
description: Held annually in mid-September.

name: Coconino County Fair
description: Held annually in September and features traditional fair exhibits, entertainment, livestock auctions, and carnival rides.

name: Dara Thai Restaurant
description: Downtown, centrally located serving decent Thai food. Get a seat by the window and view San Francisco Street while you dine. Takeout available.

name: Hunan East
description: Great Chinese food in a casual atmosphere. Takeout available.

name: Little Thai Kitchen
description: A Thai restaurant popular with locals.

name: Pato Thai
description: Downtown, another popular one with locals.

name: Fratelli Pizza
description: A pizza place that is well-loved by the locals. They have cheese, pepperoni, and pesto slices, and many specialty pies. Their pizza is hand-tossed, thin crust, brick oven pizza, like what is found back east.

name: New Jersey Pizza Company
description: Excellent choice for those looking for an all organic menu or more exotic options than the typical pizza restaurant offers.

name: NiMarcos Pizza
description: Locally owned and operated in Flagstaff for years, NiMarcos offers semi-thick crust pizza, salads and soft-serve ice cream. Go in and order your own pie or just buy a slice. Local favorite.

name: Oregano's Pizza Bistro
description: Fantastic Chicago-style pizza with a great throw-back atmosphere.

name: Pizzicletta
description: A Neapolitan style pizza place with house-made gelato. Takeout available. You can sit next door at Mother Road Brewery and order from Pizzicleta next door.

name: La Fonda Mexican Restaurant
description: Same location since the 1950s, this a well-loved Mexican restaurant with great salsa and authentic dishes. Is busy most times so expect to wait to be seated.

name: MartAnne's Cafe
description: Mexican breakfast/brunch. Awesome food, huge portions at fairly reasonable prices. Cash only.

name: Bigfoot BBQ
description: This is the place to go if you have a hankering for a pulled pork sandwich or a batch of fried okra. They even serve gourmet hotdogs. Owned by a Georgia native turned Flagstaff resident, you won't want to miss out on this!

name: Brandy's Restaurant & Bakery
description: Breakfast features quiche of the day, seven grain French toast, specialty egg dishes, homemade pastries and many other quality items. Lunch features tons of tasty sandwiches and burgers. Dinner is slightly more upscale but definitely affordable ($10-15 a plate) and features the wonderful creations…

name: Charly's Pub & Grill
description: Live blues music in the evening.

name: Diablo Burger
description: Although tricky to find and seating is rather limited, this place is one of those extraordinarily rewarding discoveries for the persistent traveler. Their burgers ($8-10) are made from range-raised beef from a ranch just north of Flagstaff, served on an English muffin with a boatload of…

name: Macy's European Coffeehouse
description: They roast their own coffee and have lots of vegan foodstuffs. A favorite amongst the hippies.

name: Silver Pine Restaurant
description: The Silver Pine Restaurant is one of Flagstaff's most popular dining choices, American cuisine.
hours: Daily for breakfast, lunch and dinner

name: Fry's
description: Has a full-service hot and cold deli, and onsite pharmacy.

name: DuBeau Hostel
description: Free wi-fi and breakfast, free coffee and tea available throughout the day.

name: Grand Canyon International Hostel
description: Free wi-fi and breakfast, free coffee and tea available throughout the day.

name: Hotel Monte Vista
description: Stay at the same hotel where some scenes of Casablanca were shot. Opened in 1927, the hotel hosted such illustrious guests as Bing Crospy, Spencer Tracy, and Jane Russell, and is widely reputed to be haunted.

name: Sleep Inn
description: 58-room hotel. Non-smoking, free breakfast and wi-fi, pets welcome. Indoor pool.

name: Weatherford Hotel
description: Noted novelist Zane Grey wrote Call of the Canyon while staying here. Widely rumored to be haunted.

name: Days Inn and Suites East Flagstaff
description: Pet-friendly lodging with king-size beds, which also provides a complimentary deluxe continental breakfast.

name: Starlight Pines Bed & Breakfast
description: 1912 Victorian style B/B. Four guest rooms with private baths, Lily with private balcony overlooking Mount Elden, Dragonfly with wood-burning fireplace.

name: England House Bed and Breakfast
description: This well-respected bed and breakfast is just four blocks from Flagstaff's historic downtown. England house was built in the early 1900s and is now furnished with antiques from the late 1800s. Breakfast is served on the bright sun porch.

name: Little America Hotel Flagstaff
description: Antique, continental flair. One of the more unique hotel experiences that Flagstaff has to offer. Free airport shuttle from 7AM-10PM.

name: Flagstaff Rental Cabin
description: 3-bedroom cabin with two king size fully adjustable beds with massage upstairs and two queen beds downstairs. Ralph Lauren bedding throughout. 55" 3D TV and fireplace in the great room.

name: Bonito Campground
description: Open beginning of May to mid-October. This campground with 44 sites is very popular and is close to Wupatki and Sunset Crater National Monuments. Drinking water, flush toilets, no hookups, trailers/RVs under 42'.

name: Canyon Vista Campground
description: Open beginning of May to mid-October, with 11 individual sites. Located near Walnut Canyon, with good views of the San Francisco Peaks. Drinking water and vault toilets, no hookups, trailers/RVs under 22'.

name: Fort Tuthill County Park Campground
description: Facilities include a few hook-up sites, picnic tables, fire rings, portable toilets, and water spigots. No water or electricity available. Reservations can be made by phone or online .

name: Lockett Meadow Campground
description: Open mid-May to mid-September, with 17 individual sites. A very popular campground with great views of the San Francisco Peaks. No water, vault toilets. Not recommended for trailers/RVs.

name: Fernow Cabin
description: A retired US Forest Service Fire Guard Station, this 3-BR log cabin housed fire fighters in the summer. The cabin can sleep up to 8 people, and is furnished with bunks, stove, and pots and pans, and vault toilet. Campers must bring their own bedding supplies. Open April 15 - November 15…

name: Kendrick Cabin
description: A retired US Forest Service Fire Guard Station, this 3-BR stone-built cabin housed fire fighters in the summer. Can sleep up to 10 people and is furnished with bunks, stove, and pots and pans; there is an outside bath house with flush toilet and shower. Campers must bring their own bedding…

name: Arizona Nordic Village
description: Offers yurts and log-sided camper cabins to rent. Yurts and cabins have bunks or mattress pads and wood stoves; no electricity or water. Wi-fi and showers are available at the main lodge, which also offers mountain bikes for rent. Reservations can be made by phone or online.

name: Flagstaff KOA
description: Spaces for trailers/RVs and tents, cabins available. Laundry, showers, wi-fi and shuttle bus; bicycles available to rent.

name: Black Barts RV Park / Steakhouse & Saloon
description: Full hookups with 50-amp service.
